sections.title: Welcome & Introduction
content: Welcome to the Advanced Message Processing System (AMPS) from 60East Technologies! 🚀 AMPS is designed for data-intensive applications with demanding requirements for low latency and high performance. It takes a nontraditional approach to messaging, storage, and analytics, built from the ground up for streaming data and highly-parallelized multicore systems.
AMPS is widely used in high-stakes environments such as:
• Trade plant operations (backtesting and historical analysis) 📈
• Risk calculations ⚡
• Elastic worker farms 🚜
• View servers 🖥️
• Message flow integration and 'shock absorbers' 🛡️
AMPS combines fast messaging with an integrated database (SOW), aggregation engine, and historical replay (Transaction Log).

sections.title: Feature Highlights
content: AMPS offers a powerful suite of features to streamline your data processing:
• **Pub/Sub Messaging**: Fast fan-out with full content filtering. 📡
• **Content Filtering**: Use SQL-92 predicates and regular expressions (PCRE2) to get exactly the data you need.
• **State of the World (SOW)**: An integrated database for current value caching and key/value storage. 🌎
• **Message Queues**: Competitive consumption with delivery guarantees. 📥
• **Complex Event Processing (CEP)**: Real-time aggregation and analytics over streaming data. 🧠
• **Historical Replay**: Record and replay message streams with full fidelity via the Transaction Log.
• **High Availability**: Integrated replication and automatic failover for enterprise scale. 🏗️

sections.title: Installation
content: Installing AMPS is straightforward. It runs on 64-bit Linux (kernel 2.6+) and contains all necessary dependencies. 🐧
1. Download the distribution to your Linux system.
2. Unpack the distribution into your desired directory (referred to as `$AMPSDIR`).
Within `$AMPSDIR`, you will find:
• `bin/`: AMPS engine binaries and utilities (like `ampServer` and `spark`).
• `docs/`: Documentation files.
• `lib/`: Library dependencies.
• `sdk/`: Include files for the AMPS extension API.
Note: AMPS client libraries (Java, C#, Python, etc.) are available as separate downloads. 📦

sections.title: Starting AMPS
content: The AMPS engine binary is named `ampServer`. ⚙️
To start AMPS, you need a configuration file. You can generate a minimal sample configuration with the following command:
`$AMPSDIR/bin/ampServer --sample-config > $AMPSDIR/amps_config.xml`
To start the server using this configuration:
`$AMPSDIR/bin/ampServer $AMPSDIR/amps_config.xml`
Once started, you should see a message indicating the version and build date. Congratulations! You've successfully cranked up the AMPS! 🎉

sections.title: JSON Messages - A Quick Primer
content: AMPS supports many message types, but JSON is the most common for evaluation and samples. 📄
JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) has two basic constructs:
• **Objects**: Key/value pairs enclosed in `{}`.
• **Arrays**: Ordered lists of values enclosed in `[]`.
JSON supports hierarchical construction, meaning values can be nested objects or arrays. AMPS uses a subset of JSON for its own command protocol (the `amps` protocol).
Example of an AMPS publish command in JSON:
`{"c":"publish","t":"test-topic"}{ "id" : 1, "message" : "Hello, World!" }`

sections.title: Spark CLI
content: AMPS provides the `spark` utility, a command-line interface for interacting with the server. ⚡
`spark` is most commonly used for ad hoc testing or simple maintenance tasks.
Common `spark` commands:
• **ping**: Test connectivity to the server.
• **subscribe**: Start a subscription to a topic.
• **publish**: Send a message to a topic.
Example ping command:
`$AMPSDIR/bin/spark ping -server localhost:9007 -type json`
This confirms that the server is listening and ready to accept JSON messages on port 9007. 🎯
